input.question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?
input.ground_truth: Master and Commander is both a really good movie, and actually historically accurate, to an extent. I've watched it, and I didn't see any particular inaccuracies about life onboard a wooden warship. The plot is based off of the British chase of the American commerce raider [U.S.S *Essex*](_URL_0_) during the War of 1812, which sailed down the eastern coast of Brazil, then up into the Pacific where it destroyed the British whaling industry. Of course, Americans don't want to see Americans as the bad guys in films, so they made the antagonist a French ship, but still.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of LEGO bricks, and you want to build a castle just like the real one from a long time ago. Sometimes, when grown-ups make big movies about old times, they use some bricks that don’t really match the real castle—they add some extra pieces or change things to make the movie more fun or easier to understand. That’s like when movies change history a little.

But sometimes, some movies try really, really hard to use the right bricks and build the castle just like it was in real life. These movies try to show things the way they actually happened. They use real names, real clothes, and even real places when they can. But it’s really, really hard to get everything just right, so even those movies might have a few mistakes.

So, yes, some big movies try to be very careful with history, but almost all of them have at least a tiny mistake here and there. But a few, like “Schindler’s List” or “Apollo 13,” try their best to be very close to what really happened!
